subject: Planned maintenance: West US rolling driver compatibility swap (staged, low-risk)

Subject: Planned maintenance: West US rolling driver compatibility swap (staged, low-risk)

Hi Nina —

We wanted to give FintechCo advance notice of a planned, low-risk maintenance activity in West US on our inference cluster that serves your production endpoints. Summary: we will perform a staged swap of a driver/KV-cache compatibility layer to address a memory fragmentation pattern that appears intermittently at very high sequence lengths. This is a rolling restart across node-groups (no full region outage).

Window and scope
- When: 2026-09-02 01:00–05:00 UTC (overnight for US-Pacific workloads)
- Scope: westus inference pool (subset of nodes pinned to your dedicated capacity)
- Expected per-node restart: ~30–60s for restart + 1–3 minutes of warmup for traffic to re-balance
- Scheduled approach: canary (2 nodes) → group-level rolling restarts (5–8 nodes at a time) → verification sweep

Expected impact
- Short-lived token-level stalls on in-flight requests for affected nodes; overall request success rate should remain >99.9% due to routing fallbacks.
- We expect a measurable but brief increase in tail latency during restarts; peak tail effects typically subside within the first 10 minutes of a group being restarted.

Mitigations in place
- Canary verification with production traffic mirror and automatic rollback on regressions.
- Auto-fallback to compatible model variant that does not use the new driver when we see more than 0.5% error increase for 5m.
- Prefix/KV cache preservation for pinned sessions where possible; for sessions that require full re-population we'll prioritize warmed nodes first.

Action for FintechCo
- No action required to stay live. If you have scheduled batch inference jobs in the window, consider moving them outside the window to avoid brief retries.
- If you'd like us to run an isolated compatibility test against a non-prod endpoint prior to the window, we can schedule it this week.

Attachments: westus-driver-compatibility-plan.pdf (high-level playbook), node-grouping.csv (nodes that host your dedicated capacity).

I'll coordinate status updates during the maintenance and post an initial postmortem within 48 hours. Please reply if you want a pre-window runbook walk-through.

Thanks,

Priya Natarajan

To: Nina Patel <nina.patel@fintechco.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-30T13:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Planned maintenance: West US rolling driver compatibility swap (staged, low-risk)

Nina — hi, Sean from Infra here. Short answers:

1) SLA exposure: we do not expect a sustained RTO or data loss. Worst-case for pinned requests: a single RPC may see a transient failure -> client retry is expected. We set route-level SLOs to 99.9% availability; during the window we expect that to hold for the vast majority of endpoints. I'll attach the rollback triggers below.

Rollback criteria (automated + manual):
- Automated rollback if error rate >0.5% above baseline for 5 consecutive minutes across the canary group (HTTP 5xx / model-level inference errors).
- Manual rollback if tail-latency P99 increases by >200ms sustained for 10 minutes in canary.
- Any customer-visible raises (multiple support tickets >3 within 15 mins) triggers immediate pause and manual assessment.

2) Streaming vs short RPCs: streaming/long-poll sessions may experience brief connection resets; our edge will attempt session rehydration where possible. For heavily stateful websockets we recommend quiescing long-lived sessions or using the fallback variant during the window.

3) Recommendation on batch job at 02:30 UTC: please reschedule to outside the window if possible. If you must run, we'll mark your job as high priority and help with retries.

Operational checks we'll run during each group restart:
- Canary health checks (inference success rate, tail latency, memory headroom)
- KV-prefill verification for pinned sessions
- Traffic shifting validation to ensure your capacity buckets remain usable

If you'd like, we can run a short 15-minute compatibility test against your non-prod endpoint on 2026-08-31 at 16:00 UTC.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.ai

Nina — thanks for the quick questions and for looping ops. Confirming next steps:

- We recommend moving your batch job out of 01:00–05:00 UTC; if you cannot, we'll coordinate with ops@fintechco.com to mark it high priority and track retries.
- We'll run the 15-minute compatibility test against your non-prod endpoint on 2026-08-31 16:00 UTC (we'll send a calendar invite).
- During the maintenance we'll provide minute-by-minute status pings to this thread and publish a short incident summary to the Drive link included after the window.

Post-maintenance: initial postmortem draft within 24–48 hours, with a final RCA if any regressions occur. Contact on-call via pager if you see any critical production impact: +1 (650) 555-0987 (Infra on-call).

If you'd like a pre-window runbook walkthrough, Marissa can lead it — Marissa, can you run 20 minutes with FintechCo tomorrow?

Thanks again — we'll be in touch with the invite.

Best,

Priya
